q: How much does a video cost?
a: It depends on what the film needs to do. Our projects have run anywhere from $1,000 to $1,000,000, and we've worked at every point in between. Most land in the thousands to tens of thousands, and bigger productions and series reach into the hundreds of thousands. Video pricing is famously foggy, so we keep it simple: tell us your goal and your budget, and we'll come back quickly with a fair number.

q: How long does a video take?
a: It can be as quick as a day or as long as a year. When you're in a hurry, we can shoot and edit a film in a single day. Projects with more research, writing, shooting and editing take longer. Either way, you'll know the schedule before we start.
We're based in Phoenix, Arizona. We shoot all over the state, work with national brands, and have traveled as far as Ireland for a story.

q: What kind of videos do you make?
a: We make brand films, documentary-style testimonials, commercials, event recaps, short cuts for social and full film series. We've made them for healthcare and medical teams, technology and manufacturing companies, product and lifestyle brands, sports and fitness, events and travel, and nonprofits and government.

We work with brands, companies, nonprofits, government programs, agencies, media outlets and other filmmakers. Some are local businesses down the street, and some are names like the NFL, UBS and Boston Scientific.

q: Can you handle the whole project, or just part of it?
a: We can do either. You can bring us in for one piece, like a shoot day or an edit, or for the whole thing from research to the final cut. When we do it all, the same crew carries your project from start to finish, so nothing gets lost along the way.

q: Who will work on my project?
a: A founder leads every project, from the first call to the final cut. You'll always know who to talk to, and it will be someone who's been there since the start.

Then we bring you a point of view on the story worth telling, one that lines up with what you're trying to get done. It's a bit like having your own research team that cares about the story as much as you do.
